Julia Roberts said she'd never forget Dolly Parton's response to her complaining on the set of the 1989 movie Steel Magnolias.

Parton, who died Tuesday in Nashville, Tennessee, appeared with Roberts, now 58, on The Oprah Winfrey Show in 1989 to promote the movie. In a clip from that appearance that has resurfaced in the wake of Parton’s death, Roberts shared that Parton had given her a crucial piece of advice during a sweltering day filming in the Louisiana summer heat.

“Everyone had ice on their wrist and was doing the whole thing, everyone was like, ‘It’s hot, can I get some water?’ And I finally just had to say, ‘Dolly, I mean, you’ve got a wig and the wool. Come on, it’s hot, sweat a little, you know? Just say ‘I’m hot,’ you know. ‘This is a drag!’” Roberts recalled to host Winfrey.

She continued: “And she said — I remember we were sitting on the porch, do you remember this? And she said to me, ‘When I was a little girl, I wanted to be famous and I wanted to be rich, and now I’m both those things. I’m not going to complain about it.’”

open image in gallery Julia Roberts has shared the piece of advice that Dolly Parton gave her at the beginning of her career, and she hasn’t forgotten it ( Sony )

open image in gallery Parton and Roberts appeared alongside Sally Field, Daryl Hannah, Shirley MacLaine and Olympia Dukakis in ‘Steel Magnolias’ ( Public domain )

Roberts said that she took the advice to never complain very seriously and that she’s “never forgotten it.”

“I thought, ‘Okay, I’m going to be quiet for the rest of the day,’” she said at the time.

“It was the way she said it, and I didn’t really do it her way, or else it’ll choke me up, but it was this thing and I’ve never forgotten it. And every time I go to complain or just kind of moan, I always hear Dolly sitting on the porch and saying that, and it kind of keeps you quiet.”

In the film, Parton played the Louisiana beauty salon owner Truvy Jones, while Roberts, who was only two years into her acting career at the time, played Shelby Eatenton-Latcherie, a young, headstrong bride.

The movie, which followed the lives of a group of women supporting each other through life’s ups and downs, also starred Sally Field, Daryl Hannah, Shirley MacLaine, Olympia Dukakis, Tom Skerritt and Sam Shepard.

After the news of Parton’s death, Roberts paid tribute to in a statement, saying: “Dolly was a magical and joyous human. I hold knowing her as a treasure in my life. The sun has dimmed today.”

MacLaine, 92, wrote, “God sent her to us, and she has returned home.”

“Without exaggeration, Dolly Parton was one of the sharpest, funniest, and warmest people I’ve ever met,” Hannah wrote in her tribute.

open image in gallery Dolly Parton’s most memorable film performance was portraying the Louisiana beauty salon owner Truvy Jones in ‘Steel Magnolias’ ( Tri-Star Pictures )

open image in gallery The Queen of Country, Dolly Parton, died in Nashville following a ‘brief battle with cancer,’ her representative said ( PA )

“She is just the best example of how to be a great human. I’m sure we will all continue to discover more about her humble, important, and generous altruistic charity work which, she would barely ever mention.”

Field said: “If there are truly angels on earth, then we have just lost one. Dolly Parton. There will never be another.”

“I adored her with all my heart and will always cherish our time together. Forever. Rest in peace beautiful Dolly,” the tribute continued.

The movie was just one of Parton’s big-screen roles across her illustrious entertainment career. She also appeared in movies including 9 to 5, Rhinestone and The Beverly Hillbillies.

Parton's death was announced Tuesday by her nephew Bryan Seaver, who served as Parton’s head of security. Her representative later confirmed that she had died in Nashville, following a “brief battle” with cancer, surrounded by loved ones.

Singer Miley Cyrus, Parton’s goddaughter, remembered her “Aunt Dolly” as an “angel,” saying, “I will always love her and want to make her proud.

News.title: Chelsea v Brighton LIVE: Joao Pedro nets third goal for Blues but Seagulls pull one back
News.content:
Why Chelsea Are SERIOUS Title Contenders

Chelsea will look to build on a strong start as they host Brighton in the Premier League in Xabi Alonso’s first league game in charge at Stamford Bridge.

The Blues caught the eye in their 3-2 win over Fulham in their opening game, with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro particularly impressive as the Alonso era got off to an encouraging start. It has raised hopes that a title challenge may not be out of the question – particularly with Emiliano Martinez brought in from Aston Villa to solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping woes. His Argentina teammate Enzo Fernandez has been left out today with Manchester City keen on the World Cup winner.

A tough test is never far away in the top flight, though, and Chelsea’s first home game is against a Brighton side who dismantled Aston Villa in a 4-0 win in their opener. A midweek Conference League play-off success has further buoyed morale for the south-coast club – can they claim a significant success at Stamford Bridge this afternoon?

Follow all of the latest from the Premier League clash with our live blog below:

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

News.title: Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty
News.content:
He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

News.title: Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow
News.content:
Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

They swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

However, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

News.title: England light years ahead of lamentable Pakistan
News.content:
Who needs Ben Stokes? Actually, it is hard to think of any side that would need him against this Pakistan team.

After just five days of cricket, and despite their own limitations with the bat, England are on the cusp of a series victory at Lord’s with a 261-run lead and power to add thanks to the prowess of a seam attack that has emerged quickly from the shadow of its former captain.

It will take longer to feel the full effects of Stokes’s absence. When England need a spinner in the side, they will miss the seam-bowling all-rounder to balance the XI. There will be times when they are up against it on a flat deck on a boiling day and be desperate for Stokes’s sheer will to win. It is still hard to think he will not play some part in the Ashes next summer.

For the final two years of his career it was Stokes’s bowling that was top class, his batting having become ordinary. But with bowlers of the quality of Ollie Robinson, Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson gelling, England are more than making up for Stokes’s retirement. This bowling attack against Pakistan’s batting was a complete mismatch.

Joe Root has stepped into Stokes’s shoes confidently, laying down the law off the field and tactically he has been spot on, although Pakistan have hardly stretched him. The only stir they have made since arriving was the stink they kicked up over Sky Sports’ interview with Imran Khan’s sons.

Conclusions are impossible to draw with any confidence against such poor opponents. Sri Lanka and West Indies two years ago put up a stronger fight in the first two Tests of their series. Tamim Iqbal scored two hundreds as Bangladesh at least landed some blows in 2010. Pakistan have managed one fifty in three innings and were bowled out for 171 and 135 at Headingley and a lamentable 110 here.

They were a batsman down at Lord’s because of a calf injury to opener Imam-ul-Haq, but only reached three figures because England dropped top scorer Azan Awais on eight; he went on to score 46.

England’s batting is hardly firing, but with a 180 first-innings lead, they could afford to be 13 for two without panic spreading. Losing Root for 24 kept Pakistan interested, but Emilio Gay toughed it out in the gloom to reach stumps unbeaten on 30; England 81 for three, light years ahead in the game.

Robinson’s astonishing figures of 13-6-11-4 set him on the way for a probable third man-of-the-match award in a row and continued his unexpected resurgence. Rarely did his pace go above 78mph, he just landed the ball time and again on a length and let movement off the seam do the rest.

News.title: I’ve lived in Norfolk for more than 30 years. Here’s how to explore England’s windswept east
News.content:
Norfolk’s vast sandy beaches are its chief draw for visitors: even on the busiest summer day there is always space for games, kite-flying or a family picnic in the dunes. Boating, crabbing, digging for cockles and wading in creeks provides hours of entertainment for all.

But there’s much more to Norfolk’s coast than its beaches. It’s also a landscape of dense pine forest and large expanses of salt marsh, which flush purple with sea-lavender in August. Birdlife is astonishingly rich, and wildflowers include yellow-horned poppies and lilac-flowering sea pea.

Inland, the undulating countryside and sleepy flint-built villages are perfect for gentle cycling, walking or touring by car. Grand stately homes make enjoyable days out, and almost every village has a sublimely beautiful medieval church at its centre.

Lively Georgian towns such as Burnham Market and Holt offer quirky shopping – and, wherever you are, you’re never far from an atmospheric pamment-floored pub serving local ales, or an excellent delicatessen selling the region’s specialities. Look out for pungent cheeses, smoked fish and salt-marsh flavoured honey.

Sports.title: Tottenham to seal Iliman Ndiaye transfer after Cody Gakpo snub with Richarlison moving to Everton
Sports.content:
Tottenham to seal Iliman Ndiaye transfer after Cody Gakpo snub with Richarlison moving to Everton

Tottenham Hotspur and Everton have reportedly agreed separate deals for Iliman Ndiaye and Richarlison after Cody Gakpo snubbed Spurs before transfer deadline day

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye are both moving away from Merseyside (Image: DARREN STAPLES, AFP via Getty Images)

Everton and Tottenham Hotspur have reportedly agreed to swap Iliman Ndiaye and Richarlison in separate deals. It is said that both players still need to agree on personal terms with their new clubs and pass medicals examinations.

‌



Ndiaye, 26, appears to be who Spurs are turning to after Cody Gakpo snubbed them for Manchester City, who are apparently in talks with Liverpool over signing the Netherlands international. Richarlison, meanwhile, has asked to leave multiple times, according to Roberto De Zerbi.

‌



It now appears he is heading back to the Blues. Spurs agreed a £60million deal with Everton four years ago.

‌



Liverpool star Cody Gakpo selects next club as talks on to complete late transfer READ MORE :

Roberto De Zerbi confirms THREE Spurs stars have asked to leave before deadline day READ MORE :

The Athletic reports that unnamed sources at both Everton and Spurs insist the deals for Ndiaye and Richarlison are entirely unrelated. Spurs forked out £50m, plus £10m in potential add-ons, to the Merseyside club for their Brazilian striker in the summer of 2022.

Roberto De Zerbi acknowledged when asked about Richarlison in his press conference after the club's 2-0 defeat to Newcastle United: "He said too many times that he wants to leave."

The forward was absent from the squad on Saturday. Ndiaye, meanwhile, played the full 90 minutes for Everton in their 1-1 draw with Bournemouth at Dean Court.

‌



View 2 Images Forwards Iliman Ndiaye and Richarlison are reportedly trading places (Image: BEN STANSALL, AFP via Getty Images)

He has featured in all three of their competitive games this season. The forward set up Thierno Barry for their second goal against Crystal Palace on the opening weekend.

Ndiaye remains contracted until the summer of 2029, yet has not put pen to paper on a fresh deal since joining from Sheffield United two years ago. He is said to have turned down several renewal offers during the last season.

‌



Richarlison has similarly never committed to a new contract since arriving at Spurs on a five-year deal. His current agreement is due to run out at the end of this campaign.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

De Zerbi was quizzed on whether there was any prospect of a return for Richarlison, Kevin Danso, and Pape Matar Sarr during his post-match press conference on Saturday, after acknowledging that all three had requested a departure.

‌



He said: "I love these players, they are great guys, I have very good relationships, but if they want to leave, they have to bring the solution, the economic solution, to the club, and they can go, and we find other players."

Spurs' head coach declined about their forthcoming transfer business, saying: "No, we speak about the game today, it's not the right moment and the right day, otherwise it's like an excuse, no, I don't want excuses."

Sports.title: Arsenal complete move for record-breaking EFL wonderkid after signing Man Utd starlet
Sports.content:
Arsenal complete move for record-breaking EFL wonderkid after signing Man Utd starlet

Arsenal have altered their transfer strategy this summer with the Gunners having moved for some of the country’s most promising young footballers and they’ve announced another deal

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal have been busy in the transfer market this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal have reached an agreement to sign Cardiff City wonderkid Axel Donczew. The Gunners were linked with the youngster earlier this summer as part of their strategy to move for some of the brightest young talents across the UK and further afield.

And Donczew’s switch to North London has now been confirmed. A statement from Cardiff on Sunday read: “Cardiff City FC can confirm that an agreement has been reached for the transfer of Axel Donczew to Arsenal. Axel became our youngest player aged 15 years and 234 days old in October 2025, a record now held by Noah Anyadike.

“The Club had offered terms for Donczew to continue his development with the Bluebirds and made efforts to retain the player, but he opted to pursue a move away from the Welsh capital. We wish Axel the best of luck for the future.”

Donczew, 16, will now play a part in the Gunners’ academy with potential for first-team exposure in the future. His switch follows a number of incomings in North London over the past few days.

Igor Tyjon has been recruited from Cardiff’s Championship rivals Blackburn Rovers. After his move was made official, he said: "It feels amazing. I've waited a long time for this and I can't wait to get started.

“It's a dream come true for [my family] as well, it's always a nice feeling when you make your family happy, so I'm buzzing for them as well.

"Who doesn't want to join the champions? I can't wait to be part of the team. The pathway, the staff, the players, everything about it, it's just top. I'm excited to meet the group, meet the players, hit the ground running and have a good season."

View 2 Images Arsenal have also signed James Scanlon this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal have also signed James Scanlon from Premier League rivals Manchester United, while they are also interested in Red Devils youngster Habeeb Ogunneye.

Arsenal have also completed a deal for Vincent Joseph, who left Liverpool at the end of last season, albeit a tribunal will now decide how much the North London side will have to pay for the 16-year-old.

It’s also been a very busy summer from a first-team perspective. Arsenal have spent heavily in an effort to defend their Premier League crown.

Piero Hincapie returned on a permanent deal following an initial loan move from Bayer Leverkusen, while Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Christos Tzolis have also been recruited for big money. Arsenal remain linked with a move for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez.

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk gives verdict on Bradley Barcola transfer and warns Liverpool bosses
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk gives verdict on Bradley Barcola transfer and warns Liverpool bosses

Liverpool are set to complete the £123million signing of Bradley Barcola, with Cody Gakpo now tipped to join Manchester City before the transfer window closes next week

View 2 Images Liverpool look set to sign Bradley Barcola (Image: PSG via Getty Images)

Virgil Van Dijk has backed Liverpool's decision to land Bradley Barcola in a £123m deal, but warned allowing Cody Gakpo to leave is a mistake.

‌



Barcola will have a medical on Merseyside before signing a five-year contract, after Paris Saint Germain accepted an initial £110m deal, plus £13m in add-ons.

‌



Supporters have criticised the club's decision to land another forward - and insist new boss Andoni Iraola needs to strengthen his midfield and defence instead.

‌



But Van Dijk believes Liverpool are landing a world class talent, who will sprinkle some stardust on a team which has failed to win its first two league games of the new season. Barcola will become the second most expensive signing in the club's history.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



And Van Dijk said: "He's a good player, that's the only thing I can say. I don't think there's any doubt that a club like Liverpool is very attractive to very good players.

"This is one of the biggest clubs in the world. We all know that we're going through a little bit of a transition. You either want to be a part of it or you don't. The window is open until Tuesday, right? Let's see what happens.

"He's a player with pace. I remember a goal he scored against Chelsea. If he comes here then he will be welcomed with open arms. But until it's official, there's no point speaking about it."

‌



View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk wants Cody Gakpo to remain at Anfield

Barcola's arrival is expected to see Gakpo leave Anfield, with Tottenham and Manchester City keen on landing the Dutchman. But Van Dijk has told Liverpool bosses that selling Gakpo would be a big mistake.

When asked if he wanted the winger to stay, Van Dijk added: "What do you think? He's a quality player. I think we should keep quality players.

Article continues below

"Let's see what the next few days bring. I want him to stay not only because he's a quality player, but also because he's a friend of mine. He's very important for us."

Sports.title: Michael Carrick hits out 'lazy' Man Utd critics after nightmare start to the season
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick hits out 'lazy' Man Utd critics after nightmare start to the season

Manchester United had the worst possible start to the 2026/27 season with defeat to newly-promoted Hull City but Red Devils boss Michael Carrick is not getting too downbeat

View 2 Images Michael Carrick endured a frustrating start to the season (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has further slammed criticism that Manchester United lack passion as ‘lazy’. The Red Devils boss was left irritated after his side’s opening day defeat to Hull City.

‌



He criticised a reporter in the aftermath of the game and claimed his comments about a potential lack of passion were ‘ridiculous’. Carrick was asked about that criticism ahead of this weekend’s clash with Ipswich Town and again did not agree with the sentiment.

‌



Speaking in his pre-match press conference, he said: "It's one game. I think there's enough leadership in our dressing room that we'll have it throughout the season.

‌



"Just because we lose a game doesn't just mean leadership, or I got passion thrown at me after the game, it's not just that. You lose two set-plays like we did, changes the game."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He added: "Teams lose games, so there's different reasons. I don't have to give you the total reason, because we know what we're trying to improve on.

‌



"But I'm just saying to you, I think it's so easy and lazy to just, team loses a game, everything's wrong. This is wrong, this is wrong, not trying enough, not enough passion. It's just like the obvious answer."

And while Carrick is refusing to panic after United’s difficult start, he has told his players that they need to improve if they want to secure victory against Ipswich.

He said: "We've probably played like that and won games, and everyone goes, 'What a great team, what a great coach, what a great load of players,' when we find a way to win 1-0. So, from my perspective, when you're analysing it, it's not the feeling and just that because of the feeling.

‌



View 2 Images Carrick has refused to panic following defeat to Hull (Image: Getty Images )

"We've got to dig deeper than that and understand the details of it. And we do, don't get carried away when we win certain games because we know it's not been perfect. And sometimes when you lose games, we know what we need to improve on.

"But there's certainly things that we can be a little bit clearer on, and calmer on in certain moments, to understand that, and keep the belief that things that we'll do well, which we will do, will win us games."

Article continues below

United have spent heavily in the transfer market this summer, having added midfielders Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba to Carrick’s squad. The latter is unavailable ahead of this weekend’s game as he continues his recovery from an ankle injury he picked up with former club Brighton.

Sports.title: Nine stars will miss Man Utd vs Ipswich Town including £75m man
Sports.content:
Nine stars will miss Man Utd vs Ipswich Town including £75m man

Manchester United will be without a number of players for their Premier League clash with Ipswich Town, with nine players in total potentially missing the Old Trafford showdown

View 3 Images Michael Carrick needs a victory to breathe life into Manchester United's campaign (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images)

Manchester United and Ipswich Town will be without nine players between them for their Premier League showdown. Michael Carrick's men are desperate to recover from their shocking start to the new campaign.

‌



They endured a thumping 2-0 defeat at the hands of Hull City, who were favourites to be relegated before the match. United have since completed the capture of Carlos Baleba for £70million from Brighton and Hove Albion, but he is set to be one of the major absentees.

‌



Meanwhile, they cannot afford to lose focus as Ipswich kicked off their campaign with a victory over Sunderland, despite being written off as heavy underdogs. Ahead of Gary O'Neil's side making the trip to Old Trafford, Mirror Football examines who will be unavailable for both clubs.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Carrick confirmed Amad Diallo will play no part in the visit of the Tractor Boys as he continues his recovery from a minor injury picked up in training. When pressed for an update on the Ivorian, who was also absent for the Hull defeat, Carrick said: "Amad won't be involved, he'll be out for a little bit longer."

Mason Mount will likewise remain on the sidelines for the clash against the East Anglians. Carrick did offer encouragement over his fitness, saying: "Mase is back around the group, he trained this week, so a real positive."

‌



Despite his arrival, the United boss also confirmed that Baleba is unlikely to be fit enough to feature against Ipswich. The Reds manager said: "He's got a little ankle issue, so maybe a couple of weeks or so, three weeks. We knew that before. It's no major issue. It'll be great to have him back."

View 3 Images Baleba recently arrived for £75m (Image: Manchester United, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Long-term injury absentee Matthijs De Ligt remains sidelined, but is edging ever closer to full fitness. Carrick offered an update on the Dutchman, saying: "Matta's obviously been out for a long period of time.

‌



"But he's training and it's great to have him back. He won't be involved, but he's in good shape and moving in a good direction, so that's a good bonus for us really, at this stage, to have him back."

While he would not have been in contention to start, backup goalkeeper Tom Heaton will also miss the fixture after sustaining an injury during the pre-season friendly against PSG. Carrick is yet to put a timeframe on the shot-stopper's return.

View 3 Images Philogene is an absentee for Ipswich (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



Ipswich are without four players. Jaden Philogene is side-lined with an ankle problem and was absent for the win over Sunderland.

Florentino Luis is ruled out with a calf injury, having also missed the clash against the Black Cats. Azor Matusiwa, another player absent last week, will sit out once more with a thigh complaint.

Jack Taylor remains on the treatment table with a knee injury, having also been unable to play in the Premier League opener.

Sports.title: Itauma unlikely to receive Hrgovic rematch
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma is unlikely to receive an immediate rematch with Filip Hrgovic after his world heavyweight title defeat.

The 21-year-old British contender inflicted a second round knockdown on Hrgovic, but then tired dramatically before being stopped in the ninth round at The O2 in London on Saturday night.

Itauma could now be forced to wait for another world title fight as no 1 contender Frank Sanchez is mandatory challenger for the IBF title after initially agreeing a deal to allow Itauma vs Hrgovic to go ahead first.

Hrgovic is also obliged to face Sanchez before he can pursue a unification bout against fellow champions such as Agit Kabayel, Daniel Dubois and Murat Gassiev.

Image: Moses Itauma (right) is back home after being taken to hospital. Pic: PA

Sanchez's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports: "Per the IBF, no intervening bout, including unification bouts, are permitted prior to the satisfaction of Frank Sanchez's mandatory.

"That said, Queensberry is going to be our partner on Frank's next bout, presumably versus Hrgovic, and we will discuss that in the coming days with Frank and George Warren.

"For eight rounds Moses was brilliant. He will be back better, much like Daniel Dubois after his first loss.

Image: Manager Mike Borao (second from right) also guides the careers of Aaron and Stephen McKenna (Photo by Cooper Neill/Zuffa Boxing)

"I spoke to Frank Sanchez and [his trainer] Eddy Reynoso immediately following the bout. Both are ready and excited for Hrgovic next.

"In the meantime, congratulations to my friends [manager] Keith Connolly and Filip Hrgovic. Keep the title warm, because Frank Sanchez is coming."

Sports.title: Spurs and Everton in advanced talks over Ndiaye and Richarlison
Sports.content:
Tottenham and Everton are in advanced talks over transfers for Iliman Ndiaye and Richarlison.

A potential fee of £60m for Ndiaye - who has rejected multiple new contract offers from Everton - is being discussed, with conversations over personal terms around a switch to north London also ongoing.

Ndiaye, who has scored 17 goals in 74 appearances since joining Everton from Marseille two seasons ago, has also been of interest to Manchester City, but Cody Gakpo - whom Spurs had also targeted - now looks most likely to move to the Etihad.

Image: Iliman Ndiaye has also been on Man City's target list for a new forward

Everton want to re-sign Spurs striker Richarlison, with a fee of £35m being discussed.

Folarin Balogun is another forward option Everton are considering, but, as things stand, their full focus is on their former player.

Image: Richarlison has scored 32 goals in 134 appearances for Tottenham

Richarlison left Merseyside in 2022, joining Antonio Conte's Spurs side in a £60m deal, but has had a frustrating time at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi admitted on Saturday that Richarlison - who scored 53 goals in 152 games for Everton - was one of three players who has asked to leave before the deadline.The other two are Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr.

De Zerbi revealed Richarlison, who is in the final year of his contract, was left out of Saturday's squad for the 2-0 home defeat to Newcastle because he had asked to leave "too many times".

"Richarlison, I don't know. He said too many times he wants to leave," De Zerbi said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United.

De Zerbi also wants to sign a new forward before the deadline. Chelsea's Pedro Neto has also been on their radar but it looks like they are moving for Ndiaye.

Spurs have spent more than £300m already in this summer's transfer window. Omar Marmoush was the most recent arrival on a loan with an obligation to buy, joining former Manchester City team-mate Savio at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after the Brazilian signed in an £85m deal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Redknapp looks back at Savio's stunning debut for Tottenham against Charlton.

Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Jan Paul van Hecke arrived earlier this summer for combined fees of £237m. Spurs also added Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi on free transfers.

Everton continue Grealish talks with Man City

Everton are continuing talks with Manchester City over another deal for Jack Grealish.

The structure of the deal remains quite fluid at this stage, Sky Sports News understands, with Grealish in the final year of his City contract.

Grealish was absent as City beat Crystal Palace 4-1 at Selhurst Park on Friday night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Michael Bridge provides the latest update on Jack Grealish, after Enzo Maresca remained tight-lipped over the midfielders' future at the club.

Sky Sports News reported earlier this month that Sunderland were exploring a potential move for the forward who spent last season on loan at Everton.

Asked about Grealish's absence, Maresca said: "I had a chat with Jack [Thursday]. Again, we'll see what happens in the next 48 to 72 hours. We'll see."

Forest move for Armstrong breaks down after fans make feelings clear

Nottingham Forest's proposed move for Harrison Armstrong from Everton has broken down.

After receiving an approach from Forest, who were willing to pay £40m for the 19-year-old midfielder, Sky Sports News understands the board is unanimous in its decision to not sell the player.

Speaking after Saturday's 1-1 draw at Bournemouth, Everton manager David Moyes said it would be a "club decision" whether Armstrong would be sold.

Asked if the bid for Armstrong should be accepted, Moyes said: "It's not really a question for just now. It will be a club decision."

Academy graduate Armstrong started on the south coast to make his 24th Everton appearance.

Travelling fans made clear their feelings on the future of the England U19 international, repeatedly chanting that a sale would leave the club with "a riot" on their hands.

"You always have to consider supporters; supporters aren't always wrong," said Moyes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Bournemouth and Everton.

"Managers have to make decisions on players sometimes and they feels like huge decisions. But there's sometimes bigger decisions to be made and the club will, I'm sure, make what they think is the right one.

"If I'd say something to them [the fans], I'd say their manager's an Evertonian."

Sports.title: Hrgovic: Itauma is 'amazing' but boxed like an 'amateur'
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic praised Moses Itauma after his shock ninth-round stoppage but said his opponent had boxed “like an amateur”.

Hrgovic, 34, became Croatia's first world heavyweight champion at The O2 on Saturday night to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title.

Itauma, 21, who was unbeaten coming into the bout, was dominant in the first six rounds after landing a string of accurate blows.

But he became visibly exhausted as the fight progressed and he failed to find a way past Hrgovic's durable chin, with the seventh round being the first time in his career he had been past six rounds.

The Croatian then pounced in the ninth round, which forced the Brit's corner to throw in the towel.

Following his win, Hrgovic hailed Itauma as the most talented fighter in the heavyweight division but said his boxing reminded him of the amateur ranks.

'I saw he was gassing'

Hrgovic said: "Let me be honest, he's amazing. I didn't know it was going to be so hard, I thought I was going to handle him easier.

Image: Hrgovic celebrates securing his IBF World Heavyweight title

"I was losing all the rounds. The kid is amazing, he was so fast, you don't see his punches coming.

"He doesn't hit so hard but he's fast. But since the first (round) I saw he was gassing out, he was boxing still like an amateur.

"He's inexperienced, I saw he was gassing out and I knew my only chance was to stay there to make him tired, to keep coming and to maybe stop him later on. That's what I did.

"I came to London, his hometown, against the most talented guy in the division and I beat all the odds.

Image: An exhausted Moses Itauma (right) couldn't maintain the pace that won him the first six rounds

"I want to be considered the best heavyweight in the world, and this is my time. I am the best. I am the present and he is the future.

"I want to fight for unification against Dubois or Agit Kabayel. I want to go for unification, that's what I want."

Itauma came into the fight lauded as one of the sport's brightest young talents after some early knockout wins.

But he will have to work on pacing himself for fights that go beyond the halfway point against durable opponents like Hrgovic.

Itauma taken to hospital but now home

Itauma was carried from the ring on a stretcher and taken to hospital following the stoppage as a precautionary measure.

On Sunday morning, a statement from Queensberry Promotions confirmed he had since left hospital and was home with his family.

The spokesperson said: "Moses is well. He left the hospital last night and is back at home with his family."

Promoter Frank Warren had earlier said: "That's what we always do to make sure because the most important thing is the boxer's health.

Image: Frank Warren said it would take some time for Itauma to bounce back. Pic: PA

"He's there and he's in the best place. We'll see what happens when I've got a report. We'll obviously let everybody know.

"He's done something to his leg as well and he was quite tired. It was a high-paced, fast fight for both the guys. It was just edge of your seat stuff all the way through."

Itauma came into the fight hoping to be crowned Britain's youngest ever heavyweight world champion, but Warren said it was now unclear what his next move would be.

Warren added: "I don't know what he's going to say. I'm sure he's a fighting man. He showed that right to the end. At the end, that's the type of fight it was - they were standing there just letting bombs go.

Image: Moses Itauma (right) is back home after being taken to hospital. Pic: PA

"I don't even know how he feels mentally. Mentally, he's going to be completely down. We're going to have to talk to him and lift him and see what he's like.

"It's going to take some time. He's going to have a nice break. It's not even the time to talk about it with him at the moment.

"It's something we're probably doing in two weeks or even a month's time, see where we go with it."

Hrgovic must now take on the IBF's mandatory challenger Frank Sanchez.

Sports.title: US Open key questions: Is Alcaraz fit? Will Sabalenka make history?
Sports.content:
The US Open, of all the four slams, is notoriously the hardest to predict the winners of as it falls at a time of year when eight months into the season the players are more likely than not nursing aches and pains with their bodies battered from the grind of the tour.

It's also played on a surface where more players fancy their chances; many have love-hate relationships with clay and grass but hard courts are their bread and butter.

The US Open is now a three-week event, week one is fan week, which this year saw five-time champion Roger Federer return for an exhibition, Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik win their first Grand Slam title after being crowned mixed doubles champions - in a competition that saw a return to Flushing Meadows of six-time champion Serena Williams - and the qualifying competition, which started with 15 Brits in the draw.

The main draw starts on Sunday and contains nine Brits, with a record five coming through qualifying. The men's competition is headed up by Sascha Zverev in the absence of Jannik Sinner [knee injury] and the women's by world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka.

In terms of questions to be asked, there are five main ones...

How will the wrist of returning champion Carlos Alcaraz hold up under the pressure of best-of-five-set Grand Slam play? Will 39-year-old Novak Djokovic finally get his hands on Grand Slam title No 25? Can an American finally win the men's title in New York? The last to do it was Andy Roddick in 2003. Can Aryna Sabalenka make history and win the US Open title for a third consecutive year? It's something that hasn't been done since Serena Williams in 2012-14. And maybe more importantly... who will end the tournament as world No 1, with four players in the running?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alexander Zverev heads into the US Open having lost to Tommy Paul at the Cincinnati Open

If we break down the draws starting with the men, the top half is headed up in the absence of Sinner by Zverev, top seed at a Grand Slam for the first time and with a major title under his belt having won the French Open earlier this year.

The draw has been kind to the German, who will fancy his chances and comes into the tournament with an 18-2 record at Grand Slam level this year.

The question, as always, is how will he cope with the pressure having fallen early in both Masters 1000 events in the lead-up as the top seed.

Working from top to bottom, the second quarter is headed up by the Australian and sixth seed Alex de Minaur, projected to meet Zverev in the quarter-finals. He might not have Djokovic or Alcaraz in his section but he does have former finalist Taylor Fritz, French Open finalist Flavio Cobolli and last year's semi-finalist Felix Auger-Aliassime.

The bottom half is absolutely stacked and features all five former US Open champions in Alcaraz, Djokovic, Daniil Medvedev, Stan Wawrinka and Marin Cilic.

Working our way down next up is Djokovic's quarter, which features Medvedev, finalist in Cincinnati Francis Tiafoe, finalist in Canada Brandon Nakashima, and a second-round meeting with one of Wawrinka or Matteo Berrettini. That's before any talk of a meeting with Alcaraz - the defending champion who heads up the final quarter.

The seeds in the Alcaraz section include winner in Canada, Ben Shelton, winner in Cincinnati, Arthur Fils, Alexander Bublik, Tommy Paul and big-hitting Roman Safiullin, who has beaten him before and is, for me, one of his toughest tests for the Spaniard having not played a singles match since April.

Into the women's draw with each quarter containing very different stories...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open final between Aryna Sabalenka and Amanda Anisimova in 2025

The main story involving Sabalenka in the first quarter who is not only looking to try and become the first woman since Serena Williams to win three consecutive US Open titles but she's also trying to hold on to the world No 1 ranking.

On paper her draw isn't too bad until the quarter-finals, where she could face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

The worry is Sabalenka's lack of form going 17-7 since April and not having won a title since March. She is without a Grand Slam title so far in 2026 and is looking vulnerable.

The second quarter is headlined by Jessica Pegula who is in contention to end the tournament as world No 1. For that to happen, the former finalist would need to win the title; nothing less would do.

Dangers lie around every corner for Pegula with Elina Svitolina, Karolina Muchova and Sorana Cirstea in her section and a second-round meeting with one of former Australian Open Champion Sofia Kenin or two-time US Open Champion Venus Williams.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Cincinnati Open final between Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula

Former US Open champion and current Cincinnati champion Coco Gauff heads up the top of the bottom half; she also has a chance of reaching world No 1, but only if she wins the title.

Lying in wait for her in the third quarter are last year's finalist Amanda Anisimova, French Open Champion Mirra Andreeva, Washington champion Alex Eala, and a potentially tricky early meeting with Paula Badosa.

And finally, to what surely is the toughest quarter of the draw with Elena Rybakina, Iga Swaitek, Naomi Osaka, Madison Keys and Belinda Bencic.

Rybakina will be the new world No 1 if she reaches the semi-finals, that is in her hands. What isn't is the left ankle/Achilles injury that she has been managing for a while, but flared up in Cincinnati forcing her to withdraw in her match against Swiatek. She has looked tentative in practice, so only time will tell if it will hold up to allow her to reach world No 1 for the first time in her career.

What about British interest?

Image: Arthur Fery lost in the Winston-Salem Open final on Saturday

When it comes to the Brits, a word on Arthur Fery, who in his second tournament since reaching the semi-finals of Wimbledon this summer, reached the final of Winston-Salem - losing out to third seed Ignacio Buse in the title decider.

Perfect preparation for Fery who has had a whirlwind summer and now heads to New York as the British No 1 thanks to that run.

The Brit will be making his debut at the US Open and it's a tough one up against 13th seed Lorenzo Musetti.

Musetti recently found some form in Cincinnati but isn't long back from a back injury, so Fery will fancy his chances.

Fery sits in the top quarter draw with top seed Zverev. Also in that section is Jan Choinski, who takes on the Dutchman Botic Van De Zandschulp.

And the other Brit to qualify on ranking is Cameron Norrie, who is in the bottom half with Alcaraz. He is the 29th seed and faces the Frenchman Luca van Assche, for the right to take on Miomir Kecmanovic or Dennis Shapovalov in round two.

In total, there are nine Brits in the main draw and for the first time at the US Open five having come through qualifying.

Among them is Toby Samuel, the world No 110, who will make his US Open main draw debut, with the 23-year-old having drawn the Czech Tomas Machac, the world No 58.

Harry Wendleken is also set for his debut after playing nine sets and nine hours to reach the main draw, and his reward is the 21st seed Luciano Darderi. Jacob Fearnley, in as a lucky loser for his second US Open appearance, will take on the Spaniard Martin Landaluce.

Image: Katie Boulter faces American wild card Carol Young Suh Lee

In the women's draw, Katie Boulter was the only direct entrant and has been handed a good first round up against the American wild card Carol Young Suh Lee.

Lee is 24, sitting at her career-high ranking of 140, and will be making her Grand Slam main draw debut.

Should Boulter win, then more than likely she will face US Open mixed doubles champion and Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova in round two.

Joining Boulter through the qualifying route is Harriet Dart, who beat Heather Watson in the final round to set up a meeting with the American and world No 54 Peyton Stearns, who she recently played and lost to in Cincinnati, but did beat the American in US Open qualifying in 2021.

And Fran Jones, who for a second year running has secured qualification into the main draw where she will face Magda Linette of Poland in what will be a first meeting between the two.

Serena will return...

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Alcaraz and Serena Williams walked out to an incredible atmosphere at the US Open mixed doubles event

Also a reminder that we haven't seen the last of Serena Williams at the US Open this year.

After playing with Alcaraz in the mixed doubles she is teaming up with sister Venus in the doubles after getting a wild card.

The two-time US Open doubles champions last played a Grand Slam together in 2022 at Flushing Meadows.

And just a word on the prize money, which has risen again this year: the men's and women's singles champions will get $5.5m (£4.7m) each and for reaching the first round it's a guaranteed $140,000 (£120,000).

And the winners are?

Image: Naomi Osaka stunned at Wimbledon. What will she reveal at the US Open?

I have left it as late as possible, and I'm still not convinced, but for who's going to win.

I will say Zverev to win his second Grand Slam title. It was tough to go against him once I saw what looks like a very favourable draw and for the women I am going outside of those who could end the tournament as world No 1 and pick Naomi Osaka to win her third US Open and first here since 2020.

From Sunday, the Sky Sports Tennis team will be back together for 15 days of wall-to-wall action with every ball of every match on every court available for you to enjoy.

Hear from Martin Navratilova, Tim Henman, Marion Bartoli, Laura Robson, Ryan Harrison and Naomi Broady to name just a few.

We look forward to your company this Sunday from 3pm live from New York.

The US Open is live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App. You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: Emiliano Martínez finally gets his Villa exit with £7.5m move to Chelsea
Sports.content:
Chelsea have completed the signing of the Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez. The 33-year-old, who has been agitating to leave Villa for the last two summers, has finally got his wish as he has moved for £7.5m, signing a three-year contract at Stamford Bridge.

Martínez, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina and twice secured the Yashin Trophy for the best goalkeeper, is set to displace Robert Sánchez as Chelsea’s No 1 goalkeeper.

“I’m delighted to be at this football club,” Martinez told their website. “Coming to Chelsea, for me and my family, was an easy decision to make and I’m just over the moon – I can’t wait to get started. I want to be successful here. I’m someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it’s a football club that wins titles, so I think it’s a good match.

“I’m all passion and I play with my heart. I will give 100% every game, every training session to make the club, my teammates and the supporters proud.”

Martínez became the latest high-profile player to leave Villa, following Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne out of Villa Park, with Ollie Watkins also set to make an exit. The Argentinian joined Villa in 2020 and was a key player in their rise to the top table of English football, culminating in last season’s Europa League success. He had tried to leave last summer but a move never materialised and another exit attempt fell through this month when a deal with Juventus collapsed.

Villa said in a statement: “Emi joined the club from Arsenal in 2020 and has been a commanding presence in goal throughout his time at the club, which culminated in him helping Villa win the Europa League in May. He earned his first international caps while at Aston Villa, going on to win two Copa América titles and a World Cup with Argentina. He was also twice named the world’s No 1 one goalkeeper, picking up successive Yashin Trophies in 2023 and 2024 as well as two The Best Fifa Football awards.

Sports.title: No country for old men: Premier League grind is why managers are getting younger
Sports.content:
One of the problems with getting older is that you’re never quite sure whether it’s you or them. Is the world really changing, or is it just you, struggling to adapt? There’s a milestone in life, probably as you’re contemplating university or a first job, when you realise you’re watching a footballer who is younger than you. Then, 15-20 years later, you realise you’re watching a manager who is younger than you. And 15-20 years after that, especially if you’re watching the modern Premier League, you realise that almost every manager is younger than you.

At which you do two things: give thanks for David Moyes; and check to see whether it’s actually happening, or whether this is just the football equivalent of the policemen-getting-younger cliche.

It turns out it is true. Managers used to be ashen-faced men with nicotine-grey hair dressed in the sports jackets of grim experience. They spoke with a rasping melancholy of the depths of human fallibility and of fates that were not to be trusted. Now they’re trim, sprightly figures in T-shirts, convinced that analytics can explain the world.

There are fewer Premier League managers now aged 50 or over than at any point in the past 20 years: only four, and two of those have only just made it over the threshold. Moyes is 63 (three months younger than José Mourinho, which, like Aberdeen being further west than Bristol, is a fact both true and too counterintuitive to be worth believing). Then there is Unai Emery at 54, Oliver Glasner at 52 and Régis Le Bris at 50. Most Premier League managers are in their 40s, with the youngest two Matthias Jaissle, 38, and Fabian Hürzeler, 33.

This is not coincidence; rather it seems the result of two interconnected trends. Even at the turn of the century, when Mourinho was starting out, it was unusual for a manager not to have played the game to at least a reasonable level, which meant they were starting their managerial careers in their mid-thirties. That’s still the route many take – Andoni Iraola, Michael Carrick, Gary O’Neil or Álvaro Arbeloa, for instance.

View image in fullscreen Andoni Iraola’s first appointment as head coach was at AEK Larnaca in 2018, aged 35. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

But there’s also a recognition, to use Arrigo Sacchi’s phrase, that a jockey does not need first to have been a horse. Coaching is regarded as a job in its own right, requiring a very different skillset to playing. Hürzeler came through the youth systems at Bayern Munich, Hoffenheim and 1860 Munich but, aged 22, in part because of an ankle injury, decided to focus on coaching.

Jaissle was a member of the Hoffenheim side that soared through the divisions to win promotion to the Bundesliga before knee and achilles tendon injuries ended his playing career at 26. The early switch into coaching seems particularly common in Germany: Thomas Tuchel and Julian Nagelsmann have similar stories.

That greater receptiveness to career coaches explains the wave of younger managers. But there are also fewer older coaches.

In part it may be coincidence: an experienced generation – Sam Allardyce, Tony Pulis and Alan Pardew – grew old together. That the process occurred just as many of their tactical characteristics – low blocks, direct play, a focus on set pieces – re-entered the mainstream may not simply be irony. The old must be cast out before it is reinvented as new; the modish cannot be represented by a 60-something football man.

But it’s also because modern management is exhausting. At Ipswich, Kieran McKenna would have his coaches present their plans to him for the day at 6am, altering anything he felt wasn’t quite right. That plan would be sent to the staff at the training ground to set up all the various pitches and drills. McKenna would then go to check everything was laid out properly. It was all extraordinarily detailed; everything was marked out, down to where players should stand when they weren’t directly involved and where water bottles would be placed.

During sessions, McKenna would walk between each unit, stepping in to offer advice and make amendments. After sessions, coaches would watch them back and report to McKenna on what could be improved before planning the next day’s drills to be presented at 6am the following morning.
