Sports.title: Featured Comment: Reintroducing refuelling would bring more negatives than positives | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses are right to argue Mohammed Ben Sulayem’s plan to reintroduce refuelling would create more negatives than positives, says reader @Stefmeister:

I wasn’t a fan of refuelling in F1 the last time and I wouldn’t be in favour of it returning.

I just always felt that it was more detrimental to the racing and never really liked the impact it had on how the races played out or how it impacted strategies.

Refuelling was always more planned and easier to read and predict with less room to adapt and change what you were doing based on how your race was playing out or what those around you were doing. You came up with a strategy the day before, went into the first stint with say 20 laps of fuel and with little room to alter that stint length the rest of your race had to be based off that.

Before and after when it was just about tyres things are a lot more reactive, harder to plan, harder to predict and you have a lot more room to change things on the fly based off how your race and what those around you are doing.

Today you can start a race looking to stop on lap 20 but if your tyres are wearing less than expected then you have scope to go a lot longer which you don’t have with refueling because if you put 20 laps of fuel in then you can’t go much longer without doing massive fuel saving.

And drivers in general have less input with refueling because yes they can do things to save fuel but they are still limited by how much was put in the tank. With tyres they can do more to extend, They can have input on changing strategy and can ask to go long if they feel tyres are holding on et cetera…

Just overall for me refueling introduces far more negatives than positives and I’d hate to see it come back.

@Stefmeister

Sports.title: Alpine confirm Colapinto will remain alongside Gasly in 2027 line-up | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Alpine has confirmed Franco Colapinto will remain at the team next year for what will be his second full season in Formula 1.

The 23-year-old joined the team last season, replacing Jack Doohan from the seventh round of the season in Miami. He ended the season point-less as Alpine struggled throughout the year with an uncompetitive car.

He has enjoyed more success this year, his first full season as an F1 driver, taking his best result so far with sixth place in the Canadian Gerand Prix. Colapinto has scored 19 points so far, putting him 12 in the championship, two places behind team mate Pierre Gasly.

The pair will remain team mates next year. “For me, having consistency is very important,” said Alpine’s executive consultant Flavio Briatore. “We are now settled from a driver point of view and I have said many times that, while this is an important piece of the puzzle, the most significant we have to get right is designing and building a fast race car which absolutely remains our number one priority.

“We have seen Franco truly grow and mature into a great driver this year. His results in Miami and Montreal especially confirmed what I already knew: Franco belongs in Formula 1 and he belongs at this team.”

Colapinto said he is “very pleased” to renew his contract with Alpine. “I feel very happy and very settled here and it’s been even better that we have made significant progress this year compared to last.”

He made his F1 debut in 2024 at Williams, replacing Logan Sargeant after the Dutch Grand Prix. The Alpine driver is the only Argentinian to race in F1 over the last 20 years and the team arranged a show run for him in Buenos Aires in April.

Sports.title: Mercedes told Antonelli he would get F1 chance before Hamilton’s exit was announced | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli has revealed how quickly Mercedes reacted to Lewis Hamilton’s decision to leave the team at the beginning of 2024.

The world championship leader said he first learned Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff intended to promote him to the team before Hamilton’s decision to join Ferrari was announced.

Ferrari announced Hamilton would join them in February 2024. Antonelli said Mercedes told him of their decision shortly beforehand.

“It’s 2024, the year I’m turning 18, it’s February, I was in Silverstone,” he said in a recent interview for one of the team’s sponsors. “I was testing Formula 3 to learn the track, because I was going to race there with Formula 2.

“I remember at the end of the day, Toto called me over to his office. And already there, I was a bit confused, because I’m like, [this] doesn’t really happen.

“So I got into his office. Obviously, it’s Toto, there’s Rosa [Herrero Venegas, PR manager] and she’s the one helping me during race weekends.

“Toto, first of all, didn’t waste any time, went straight to the point and it was like this was even before Lewis was announced. To Ferrari. So he said, look, Lewis is going to Ferrari and we were thinking to put you in the car for next year. And I’m like, ‘whoa’.”

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Antonelli had won the Formula Regional European Championship the year before. “My eyes were wide open and I was like, ‘are you kidding me?’ Because I hadn’t even started F2.

“So I had still so much to prove that I could earn that spot. And Toto was already talking about it.”

Wolff asked Antonelli if he would be ready for the opportunity. “I said, yeah, I’ve got to be ready,” Antonelli recalled.

Mercedes began a programme of F1 tests for Antonelli that year, culminating in his first appearance in an official practice session at Monza. Although Antonelli crashed five laps into the session, the following day Mercedes announced he would take Hamilton’s place in 2025.

However Antonelli had already learned of Mercedes’ decision long before that weekend.

“The official announcement came just at the start of summer break. It was, I think, just the start of August, probably, first day of August. I was at home with my family, and Toto organised this call, and where there were also all the big names from Mercedes.

“There was James Allison [technical director], Gwen Lagrue, who was the one who took me in the junior programme. There was Bradley [Lord], Rosa again, there was all of the big ones. Toto in the call went straight to the point and said he’s going to be our driver for next year. And it was an incredible moment.”

Sports.title: Why F1 team bosses believe refuelling “doesn’t add a lot to the spectacle” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has suggested reintroducing refuelling to Formula 1 as a means of making the cars run at a lower weight.

However three bosses asked about the proposal are not convinced it would improve the racing.

Racing Bulls team principal Peter Bayer, who previously worked as the FIA’s secretary general, said the idea has been studied recently and found wanting.

“When I was still working with the FIA, we had a working group with Formula 1, with Ross Brawn [former F1 sporting director] back in the days, and his team, about how to improve the entertainment, the spectacle.

“One of the big ideas of some people was refuelling. We were digging very deep into historic footage, data that we had, and it showed that other than a couple of very spectacular and dangerous images, refuelling has not done really anything for the sport because most of the overtaking suddenly took place in the pit lane. So I wouldn’t be a big fan of that because it’s proven that it actually doesn’t add a lot to the spectacle.”

Refuelling also adds complexity for fans who are trying to follow the races, said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu.

“I’m personally not a big fan of refuelling, really,” he said. “When I was watching from outside, refuelling, it’s just that the race was so difficult to understand as a spectator sitting on the stand.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Also in terms of qualifying, et cetera. I’m fond of a qualifying car being the lightest, the driver going for everything. So in short, I’m not fond of refuelling – and also the weight and cost and everything – I’m not a big fan.”

Williams team principal James Vowles, who previously headed Mercedes’ strategy division, pointed out that refuelling would take a lot of the intrigue away from pit stops.

“We could fundamentally predict exactly where the car is going to stop. You’re always going to take the car right to the end of its fuel load because that’s when it’s its fastest, which now means you can predict what’s going to happen, whether someone’s on a two or three or one, it doesn’t matter.

“Nowadays, with the exposure to the outside world, everyone will start getting that information. It actually takes quite a bit of the intrigue out of it for me.”

However he said he is in favour of trying to reduce the weight of the cars. “I’m completely in support of that,” he said. “I think going back to refuelling is not the right solution for it, however.

Vowles also admitted to having a personal reason to oppose refuelling. “It’s quite warm wearing a race suit when you’re on the pit wall, so I’d prefer not to do that again!”

Sports.title: Lester Martinez Breaks Down Luka Plantic in Ten
Sports.content:
By the middle rounds, Martinez was taking control. His body shots and sustained output forced Plantic to spend more time defending and holding. The challenger’s early bursts gave way to longer stretches in which Martinez dictated the action.

Plantic had enough offense to make Martinez fight, but he could not maintain his own work as the punishment accumulated. A heavy hook staggered him, and the later rounds brought more clean connections from the champion.

Martinez dropped Plantic in the tenth. Although the challenger got up, the referee stopped the contest shortly afterward. Plantic protested, but the knockdown followed several rounds in which the fight had been moving away from him.

Afterward, Martinez called for the winner of Canelo Alvarez versus Christian Mbilli. He described the Plantic defense as work required of him and made clear he was ready for either opponent. His draw with Mbilli gives him a reason to want that fight again, while Canelo offers the biggest payday in the division. Martinez has defended his interim belt; what remains unresolved is when he will get a shot at the full championship.

Sports.title: And The New Heavyweight Champion Of The World From Zagreb, Croatia Filip Hrgović
Sports.content:
Unlike the Brit’s previous opponents, however, Hrgović did not capitulate. On the contrary, the Croatian kept coming forward, Rocky Balboa-like, Itauma’s punches appearing to have little or no effect on him. The only danger to Hrgović was his tendency to cut easily in his fights, with cuts being the reason for the Croatian’s only loss as a professional heavyweight boxer on 01 June 2024 to now WBO Champion Daniel Dubois.

As the fight went on, Hrgović came more and more into his own. In contrast, Itauma became more and more undisciplined as the contest wore on, often gasping for air. At the end, Itauma had become so ragged that he gave up trying to outbox Hrgović, and instead engaged inexplicably in a slugfest with the Croatian, of which Itauma was never going to be the winner, considering Hrgović’s wealth of experience. And so ended Moses Itauma’s dream of becoming the second youngest World Heavyweight Boxing Champion after Mike Tyson.

It would be cruel to blame Itauma entirely for his loss. Some of the responsibility for it must lie with his trainer Ben Davison, who was supposed to be Itauma’s eyes and ears in the ring, but may not have given his fighter the right advice. In this regard, the way Itauma fought in the 9th Round beggars belief. Apart from Davison, the boxing pundits in the UK must also carry their share of the blame for the Brit’s loss. They practically all predicted a victory for Itauma. The pressure this may have exerted on young Moses to win and win convincingly may have contributed to his irregular performance in the later Rounds, especially as these so-called boxing experts foresaw Itauma beating Hrgović by early stoppage.

In the final analysis though, Filip Hrgović must be congratulated for executing his gameplan against Moses Itauma perfectly. The Croatian studied Itauma’s previous fights, and knew that the 21-year-old had not been past six Rounds. Hrgović exploited Itauma’s lack of fighting time, aware that the Brit may tire in the later Rounds, whereas the Croatian has a reputation for becoming more dangerous the longer a fight goes on. In this regard, Hrgović’s strategy against Itauma was somewhat akin to the rope-a-dope tactics the great Muhammad Ali used against George Foreman in their famous Rumble in the Jungle in October 1974, when Ali allowed Foreman to punch himself out to regain the world heavyweight title. To be compared to Muhammad Ali is a massive compliment for Hrgović, which he richly deserves.

Further, Hrgović had to overcome a brief knockdown in the 2nd Round to come on to win. In addition, he beat Itauma in his own backyard, which is a considerable achievement.

The likable Filip Hrgović thoroughly deserved his victory against Moses Itauma on Saturday night. Filip Hrgović is the pride of Croatia.

Romer Cherubim

Freelance journalist

UK

Sports.title: Mauricio Lara Stops Carlos Ornelas After Trading Knockdowns
Sports.content:
Lara, 31-3-2 (24 KOs), of Mexico City, collected his fifth consecutive victory. Ornelas, 29-6 (16 KOs), of Rosarito, Baja California, gave him an early scare before being stopped.

During the final minute of the opening round, Ornelas dropped Lara with a left to the chin. Referee Manuel Rivera administered an eight-count, but Lara recovered and returned the favor, flooring Ornelas with a right to the chin before the bell.

Ornelas beat the count but also suffered a bad cut over his left eye. Lara resumed his attack in the second round, and the contest was halted after just 42 seconds.

Jorge Mata Stops Ronaldo Ruelas

In the scheduled 10-round co-feature, Guadalajara’s Jorge Mata, 23-3-2 (15 KOs), also recovered from an opening-round knockdown to stop fellow Guadalajara fighter Ronaldo Ruelas, 18-4-2 (13 KOs), at 2:56 of the third.

Ruelas dropped Mata with a left hook to the chin in the first round. Mata took an eight-count from referee Augustine Ayala and continued.

By the third, Mata had turned the fight around, dropping Ruelas for the count to complete his comeback.

Santiago Barajas Upsets Joshua Franco

Santiago Barajas, 10-1-2 (4 KOs), defeated former WBA super flyweight champion Joshua “El Professor” Franco, 18-3-3 (8 KOs), by split decision over eight rounds.

Franco, of San Antonio, Texas, outlanded Barajas through much of the opening round. With just over a minute remaining in the second, he dropped Barajas with a three-punch combination that began and ended with a left hook to the chin. Referee Manuel Rivera administered an eight-count.

Barajas recovered and stayed in the contest. Franco had the better of the exchanges in an action-filled fourth round, while the seventh developed into a war. Both maintained a high pace through the eighth and final round, with Barajas taking the decision despite the knockdown.

Roberto Carbajal Scores First-Round Knockout

Guadalajara’s Roberto Carbajal, 3-0 (1 KO), knocked out Lenin Ulises, 5-2-1 (1 KO), of Mexico City, at 0:42 of the opening round in their scheduled six-round bout.

A left hook to the chin sent Ulises to the canvas, where referee Augustine Ayala counted him out.

Hector Carbajal Stops Aldo Aran

Hector “El Gato” Carbajal, 3-0 (3 KOs), of Guadalajara, stopped Aldo Aran, 3-2 (1 KO), of Saltillo, Coahuila, at 2:38 of the third round.

Carbajal dropped Aran with a combination to the chin in the third. Aran rose and received an eight-count from referee Augustine Ayala, but Carbajal followed with another flurry. With Aran unable to defend himself, Ayala stepped in to end the fight.

David Diamante served as the ring announcer.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma Fights Like an Amateur
Sports.content:
“I saw from the first round that he was breathing hard,” Hrgovic said at his post-fight press conference. “He throwing too much. He was fighting like an amateur, you know, and I knew I need to endure. I need to stay there. And he going to get tired, you know, and I’ll get him in later rounds.”

The British crowd gave Itauma encouragement to keep spending. Every big shot brought another roar, urging him to follow with more. Ignoring that reaction takes discipline, especially when an opponent has already been down. Itauma kept responding with attacks he could not sustain, feeding the crowd’s excitement while leaving himself increasingly exposed.

Hrgovic managed those exchanges with greater composure. He covered up through the worst stretches and answered often enough to stop Itauma from having everything his own way. That did not mean he was comfortable. His speed difficulties were real, but he resisted the temptation to match every burst. While Itauma chased the finish, Hrgovic preserved enough energy to punish him afterward.

Nor did Itauma reach the championship rounds. He was stopped before round ten began, with three full rounds still beyond him. Ben Davison’s towel followed the referee’s intervention. His own corner also wanted the punishment ended.

This was not a flawless trap laid by Hrgovic. He admitted he had anticipated an easier fight and initially struggled to connect because Itauma’s punches and counters were too fast. Surviving that speed required absorbing shots he had wanted to avoid.

Hrgovic lasted long enough to exploit the exhaustion Itauma’s earlier opponents had never forced him to confront.

His recommendation was easier fights and better pacing for Itauma. Easier opposition may rebuild confidence, but quick knockouts will not establish that he has corrected anything. He needs to learn how to end an attack without emptying himself, defend while recovering, and accept that a hurt opponent may survive.

Until then, the same vulnerability remains: Itauma becomes available to hit after doing his best work.

Sports.title: Chantelle Cameron Outworks Mikaela Mayer for Three Belts
Sports.content:
Cameron kept advancing, finding right hands at close range before increasing her body attack from the fifth round. That gave Mayer more to defend than the punches coming upstairs. Once Cameron got close, Mayer needed a way to interrupt her work and create room again. Trading there gave Cameron the kind of fight she wanted.

By the eighth, Mayer was bleeding from the nose. Cameron suffered a cut near her left eye in the ninth, but neither backed off. Both continued exchanging through the closing seconds of the tenth, with Cameron’s sustained inside work earning her the decision.

The fighters confirmed afterward that a rematch is planned, and Mayer has an adjustment to make beyond starting well behind her jab.

Lateral movement after punching and tying Cameron up before she can unload inside are possible answers. Mayer needs to make her opponent earn each approach, rather than allowing one successful entry to become a prolonged exchange.

Cameron wants their second meeting contested over three-minute rounds. Longer rounds would give her more time to sustain those attacks before the bell, but the benefit is not automatic. She would have to maintain that output, while Mayer would have more time to establish her jab and make Cameron miss.

Their first meeting rewarded Cameron’s ability to keep working at close quarters. Unless Mayer can shorten those exchanges, another fast start may leave her facing the same difficult second half.

Sports.title: Will Queensberry Risk Itauma Against Hrgovic Again?
Sports.content:
Itauma remained in distress afterward and was removed from the ring on a stretcher. Frank Warren later attributed that to a leg injury and exhaustion, but the closing sequence still showed a young heavyweight with nothing left when Hrgovic attacked.

Darshan Desai offered the sympathetic reading shared by many Itauma supporters:

“Moses Itauma will come again. He is 21 and he looked sensational at points in that fight. Just needs to work on his gas tank, and get more rounds and experience. I still think he’ll win a world title very soon.”

That may all prove true. Itauma’s career does not need to be buried after one loss at 21. Yet “coming again” should mean rebuilding, not returning to the heavyweight who left him helpless against the ropes. It could be more than a gas tank that Itauma needs for him to beat Hrgovic. Punch resistance has a lot to do with it, too. Itauma showed that he can dish it out, but he can’t take return fire nearly as well.

Queensberry Sent Him There Too Soon

Before facing Hrgovic, Itauma had completed only 31 professional rounds. He had never gone beyond the sixth and had boxed only five rounds against Jermaine Franklin in his previous contest.

Hrgovic brought more than 100 professional rounds and experience against Daniel Dubois and Zhilei Zhang. He had already fought while exhausted, hurt and under heavy pressure. None of those conditions had confronted Itauma before.

That difference took control once the fight moved beyond Itauma’s familiar territory. The early speed remained impressive, and he dropped Hrgovic in the second. Instead of treating the knockdown as part of a 12-round fight, Itauma continued pouring power into combinations against a man known for absorbing punishment.

Once Hrgovic survived, Itauma’s energy drained and no second method surfaced. There was no lower gear to conserve strength, no defensive adjustment and no way to discourage the Croatian once he began walking forward.

Itauma’s stamina problem was inseparable from his defensive collapse. He spent too much energy whenever Hrgovic was hurt, then remained in punching range with his hands low, leaving him vulnerable. Hrgovic was able to recover while landing heavy shots of his own. He showed tonight that he doesn’t have the gas tank to go for a finish against a heavyweight like Hrgovic. Itauma was throwing wildly, getting caught with right hands from Hrgovic. A second fight would invite the same problems.

The rush to make Itauma one of the youngest heavyweight champions helped create this situation. His knockout victories allowed Queensberry to promote every short night as evidence that he was ready. In truth, those quick finishes denied him the preparation he needed before meeting someone who would not disappear.

If Queensberry wants to throw Itauma back on the frontlines against Hrgovic, they could be risking his career. He looked battle-torn at the end, being stretchered out of the ring. After the way this fight ended, there’s no way of knowing how this will affect him. Given his age, he doesn’t need to fight Hrgovic again.

Pride Cannot Choose Itauma’s Next Fight

The difficulty will come if Itauma demands another chance. Queensberry spent months presenting him as the next heavyweight ruler and a fighter mature beyond his years. Losing after that buildup creates more than disappointment. The urge to erase the defeat may convince him that beating Hrgovic is the only way to recover what vanished against the ropes.

A second fight would give Hrgovic knowledge that cannot be erased. He knows he can absorb Itauma’s early attack, extend him beyond the rounds he prefers and overwhelm him once the speed and energy disappear.

Itauma’s endurance requires work, but so do his pacing, defensive discipline and ability to survive when a durable opponent refuses to fold. Those improvements come through fights and rounds, not through revisiting a frightening stoppage after one training camp.

Hrgovic has IBF mandatory Frank Sanchez waiting for him. Queensberry should allow that fight to proceed while Itauma recovers and learns how to operate after his early attack fails. If Itauma becomes the champion his handlers promised, Hrgovic may still be there later.

Sending him directly back would not prove confidence. It would show that Queensberry allowed a badly hurt 21-year-old to make a critical career decision while pride and shame were still driving him.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Breaks Moses Itauma in Ninth
Sports.content:
Hrgovic Stops Itauma in Round Nine

IBF Intercontinental champion and 2016 Olympic bronze medalist Filip “El Animal” Hrgovic, 21-1 (16), stopped WBO Intercontinental champion Moses Itauma, 14-1 (12), at 2:27 of the ninth round. The bout was scheduled for 12 rounds.

Itauma dropped Hrgovic to one knee with a left hand during the second round. Referee Howard Foster administered an eight-count before allowing the action to continue.

The southpaw’s hand speed, sharp combinations and body punching carried the next several rounds. Itauma repeatedly beat Hrgovic to the punch and built a large lead while the Croatian absorbed heavy shots without breaking.

Everything changed once Itauma crossed into territory he had never experienced as a professional. His movement slowed, his punches lost force, and his defensive shape began to disappear.

Hrgovic attacked from the opening seconds of the ninth. A right hand hurt Itauma midway through the round, and the exhausted challenger struggled to remain upright. He eventually collapsed into the corner, prompting trainer Ben Davison to throw in the towel as Foster halted the contest.

Itauma had done most of the better boxing, but Hrgovic had prepared for the portion of the fight that the younger man had never seen. The early knockouts that built Itauma’s reputation offered no evidence of how his body would respond after six hard rounds against a full-sized heavyweight who refused to leave.

Hrgovic credited his Christian faith after the comeback.

“It was not me tonight. It was Jesus Christ in me. Holy Spirit.”

The new champion admitted Itauma had outboxed him and said he did not know where the energy for his ninth-round attack came from. He also thanked trainer Abel Sanchez, manager Keith Connolly and the rest of his team for producing the best training camp of his career.

Itauma required medical attention and was removed from the ring on a stretcher after the fight. Hrgovic became Croatia’s first heavyweight world champion.

Sam Noakes Decisions Denys Berinchyk

In the co-main event, former British and Commonwealth lightweight champion Sam Noakes, 19-1 (16), defeated former WBO champion and 2012 Olympic silver medalist Denys Berinchyk, 19-2 (9), by unanimous decision over 10 rounds. The vacant WBO International lightweight title was at stake.

Noakes outworked Berinchyk during the opening four rounds as the Ukrainian returned from an 18-month absence. A right hand stunned Berinchyk during the closing seconds of the fifth.

Berinchyk had a better eighth despite eating another right hand near the bell. Noakes regained control in the tenth and closed the fight strongly.

The judges scored it 100-90, 99-91 and 98-92. Bob Williams was the referee.

Constantin Ursu Retains After Vaughan Cut

British and Commonwealth welterweight champion Constantin “The Moldovan Monster” Ursu, 16-0 (7), knocked out Ben “The Bomber” Vaughan, 12-3 (4), at 0:03 of the eighth round.

Vaughan gave Ursu a competitive fight before an accidental clash of heads opened a cut over his right eyebrow in the fifth. The injury worsened as the bout continued, while Ursu began taking firmer control during the seventh.

The ringside doctor inspected Vaughan twice. With the eye closing and the cut no longer safe, the contest was stopped before meaningful action began in the eighth. Michael Alexander was the referee.

Nelson Hysa Stops Thomas Narmo

WBA Gold and WBO Global heavyweight champion Nelson “The Albanian Eagle” Hysa, 25-0 (23) knocked out Thomas “The Last Viking” Narmo, 14-1 (14), at 0:36 of the second round of a scheduled 10.

Hysa took the first round before closing the fight early in the second. A lead right landed against the side of Narmo’s head and sent him down. Narmo beat the count, but referee Howard Foster determined that he was in no condition to continue.

Aloys Youmbi Outpoints Sherif Musah

WBC Continental cruiserweight champion Aloys Youmbi, 12-1 (9), 205¼, of Penge, South London, defeated Sherif Musah, 4-2-1 (2), 202¼, of London, by decision.

Youmbi was returning after more than a year away and had prepared to face southpaw Mike Perez before Musah accepted the fight on short notice. The switch to an orthodox opponent contributed to an awkward opening.

Through the first three rounds, Youmbi held the edge by countering the aggressive Musah. A right uppercut rocked Musah during the final 15 seconds of the third, forcing him to hold.

Musah remained competitive during the closing rounds, but Youmbi landed the cleaner punches. Referee Lee Every scored the six-round bout 60-54.

Arbnor Jashari Defeats Numan Hussain

Lightweight Arbnor “Kid Dynamite” Jashari, 10-0 (3), defeated Numan Hussain, 8-2 (2) by a six-round points decision.

Jashari rocked Hussain with a right hand during the closing seconds of the second. Hussain answered before the bell, but Jashari’s quicker combinations carried the remaining rounds.

Referee Lee Every scored it 59-55.

Guido Vianello and Moses Jolly Draw

WBC Continental Americas heavyweight champion and Italian Olympian Guido “The Gladiator” Vianello, 14-3-2 (12), drew with late replacement Moses “The Native” Jolly, 12-0-1 (8), in an eight-round bout.

Vianello bloodied Jolly’s nose with a right hand in the second. Jolly turned the fight into a rougher contest and tossed Vianello to the canvas during the fourth, although it was not ruled a knockdown.

Blood from Vianello’s left ear required an examination by the ringside doctor. Both heavyweights had success during the seventh and eighth, leaving referee Amy Pu to score the fight 76-76.

The draw reflected eight untidy but competitive rounds. Vianello delivered the straighter punches, while Jolly’s pressure and physical strength kept him in the fight.

Tony Curtis Edges Imad Naseeb

Super flyweight Tony “Lightning” Curtis Jr., 14-1 (3), 112½, of Woolwich, London, defeated Imad Naseeb, 8-1 (2), 111½, of Warrington, over six rounds.

Naseeb switched between southpaw and orthodox while pressing forward through the first four rounds. Referee Lee Every warned him several times for punches behind the head.

During the fifth and sixth rounds, Naseeb trapped Curtis in a corner and knocked out his mouthpiece in each round. Curtis, trained by Roy Jones Jr., continued moving and countering well enough to take the decision.

Every scored it 58-56.

Frankie Wood Stops Callum Lee

Featherweight southpaw Frankie Wood, 5-0 (2) stopped Callum Lee, 8-1 (1), at 1:21 of the sixth and final round.

Lee’s left eye began swelling during the opening round, although much of Wood’s work was directed toward the body. Lee countered effectively and remained competitive through five.

Wood increased the pressure in the sixth and dropped Lee with a lead right hook to the chin. Lee rose, but referee Amy Pu waved off the contest after deciding he was unable to continue safely.

Sam King Outpoints Jack Swallow

Middleweight Sam King, 7-0-1 (1), defeated Jack “Mad Dog” Swallow, 4-13-1 (1), by points.

Returning after six months away, King pressed the action and kept Swallow on the defensive for most of the contest. King’s work rate and cleaner punches decided the rounds.

Referee Amy Pu scored it 40-36.

Zayn Ahmed Stops Liam Fitzmaurice

Super featherweight southpaw Zayn “The Hurricane” Ahmed, 3-0 (1), 130¼, of Slough, stopped Liam Fitzmaurice, 0-19, 132½, of Tyldesley, Lancashire, at 2:47 of the second round of a scheduled four.

During the final minute of the second, Ahmed landed a right to the body that dropped Fitzmaurice. Referee Amy Pu immediately stopped the bout.

Hassan Ishaq Decisions Enzo Munoz

Super bantamweight Hassan “Shooter” Ishaq, 4-0 (3), defeated Enzo “El Bulls” Bahiano Munoz, 4-17-4 (2), over four rounds.

Ishaq’s punches caused swelling around Munoz’s left eye during the opening round. Munoz switched to southpaw and remained durable, producing his best attack during the closing seconds of the fourth.

Munoz had been stopped only once and again lasted the distance. It was Ishaq’s first professional bout to reach the scorecard.

Referee Lee Every scored it 40-36.

Thomas Treiber served as ring announcer.

Sports.title: Mauricio Lara Survives Knockdown, Stops Carlos Ornelas
Sports.content:
Ornelas struck first, dropping Lara early. That gave the favorite an immediate test of his recovery and briefly put the underdog in position to wreck Lara’s winning streak.

Instead, Lara (31-3-2, 24 KOs) recovered and put Ornelas (29-6, 16 KOs) down late in the round. The bell gave Ornelas a break, but he had lost the advantage he earned only moments earlier. Dropping Lara had not taken the danger out of the exchanges.

There was little attempt to slow things down when the second began. Both resumed throwing, and Lara hurt Ornelas before pressing for the stoppage. A bad cut above Ornelas’ eye accompanied the punishment, and the referee halted the contest shortly into the round.

That trip to the canvas keeps this from being a routine demolition. Lara was vulnerable enough to give Ornelas a chance, but his ability to recover and return damaging punches decided the fight. Ornelas could put him down; keeping him under control afterward was another task entirely.

A championship at 130 pounds remains Lara’s goal, as Matchroom outlined before the fight. This result keeps that pursuit moving, although the opening round gives better opponents something to study.

Five consecutive victories give Lara a stronger case for better opposition. Saturday also showed the risk he carries into that next step: his power can rescue him from trouble, but he is still giving opponents opportunities to land first.

Ghana News.title: 7 feared dead at reclaimed mining site in Atiwa East
Ghana News.content:
Seven people are feared dead after being trapped at a reclaimed mining site at Asaman Tafo in the Atiwa East District of the Eastern Region.

A police-led evacuation operation has since been completed, with all seven individuals reportedly found unresponsive.

Details surrounding the circumstances of the incident are yet to be made public.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Immigration Service removes 1,055 street beggars from the streets of Accra and Kumasi
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) has removed 1,055 migrant street beggars from the streets of Accra and Kumasi as part of an operation targeting undocumented foreign nationals.

The exercise follows directives from the Minister for the Interior, Mubarak Mohammed Muntaka, aimed at addressing the presence of undocumented migrants and street beggars in major Ghanaian cities.

The operation forms part of ongoing efforts by authorities to address concerns over street begging and human trafficking, particularly in urban centres such as Accra.

The individuals identified as illegal immigrants are currently being processed for repatriation to their respective home countries.

The development forms part of broader efforts by the Ghana Immigration Service to enforce the country's immigration laws and regulate the presence of foreign nationals without valid documentation.

Ghana News.title: Ghana @70: Litina outlines support services for diaspora visitors seeking to reconnect with Ghanaian roots
Ghana News.content:
Ghana's planned 70th Independence anniversary celebrations are expected to draw renewed attention to people of African descent seeking to reconnect with their ancestral roots, including those who may be eligible to pursue Ghanaian citizenship.

Thus, travel and tour company Litina Travel says it is offering a range of support services for members of the African diaspora planning visits to Ghana or seeking to settle in the country.

The company's services include heritage tours designed to help visitors explore Ghana's history and cultural connections, as well as support for people considering longer-term relocation.

Under its 'Reconnect with your roots' - a 14-day Black Heritage Connect Tours programme, participants are expected to have opportunities to engage with aspects of Ghana's history and culture while reconnecting with their African heritage.

Litina Travel says its wider support services cover housing assistance, relocation support, diaspora integration, and concierge services.

The company also provides referrals for legal and immigration matters, alongside assistance relating to banking and financial services. Other areas of support include guidance for employment, business establishment, and citizenship-related processes.

The services come as discussions continue around Ghana's relationship with the African diaspora and efforts to encourage people of African descent to reconnect with the continent.

Ghana has, in recent years, positioned itself as a destination for members of the diaspora through initiatives aimed at promoting tourism, investment, and cultural reconnection.

Litina Travel said people seeking further information about its heritage tours and other support services can contact the company on +233 244 260 789.

The company says its services are intended to support visitors and prospective residents as they navigate the practical and cultural aspects of reconnecting with Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Boat carrying nearly 270 people capsizes off northern Cyprus
Ghana News.content:
A passenger boat with nearly 270 people on board has capsized off northern Cyprus, with a search and rescue operation under way.

Turkey's interior ministry said the passenger ship was carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members when it began taking on water after departing Kyrenia bound for Turkey.

Murat Senkul, the mayor of the coastal town, told CNN Turk that 159 of those aboard had been reached. "The situation is very serious," he said.

Local television has broadcast images of the upside-down ferry in the water, with people wearing life vests atop its hull.

Helicopters and coastguard boats have been dispatched to the scene, while ambulances have been stationed on the beach.

The transport minister of the self-proclaimed Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), Erhan Arikli, told local media 100 passengers had been taken to shore.

The TRNC, which is recognised only by Turkey, controls the northern third of the island of Cyprus, which has been divided since 1974.

Ghana News.title: Survivalist dropped into Arctic Circle alone with just 10 tools for TV show
Ghana News.content:
Dropped in the Arctic Circle with just 10 tools and a camera, Andrew Price faced loneliness and lit fires to cook and boil water.

Despite worries of grizzly bears and the extreme cold, the 51-year-old has become the first Welshman to compete in the US TV show Alone: World Championship.

"I've always wanted to push myself in a really cold environment, it doesn't get colder than the Arctic Circle so it felt like the perfect place to go," Price said.

"It was definitely the most physically and mentally challenging thing I've ever done."

Growing up in the suburbs of Swansea, Price's grandad introduced him to foraging for seaweed, mussels and blackberries on the Gower Peninsula.

When he was eight, his grandad used to take him on walks in Mumbles to collect periwinkles and boil them for food.

"As a kid, it seemed like a normal thing to do but only later on in life that I realised not everyone did that," Price said.

With his dad, he used to go out kayaking and fishing around Mumbles Head, trying to catch mackerel and bass.

This later introduced him to bushcraft, which includes skills such as hunting in a natural environment.

After leaving school, Price went on an expedition to Malaysia where he spent several months living with the indigenous people of Peninsular Malaysia, Orang Asli.

He described the experience as "very immersive" as he learned what it was like to live in a jungle and hunt with blowpipes.

It exposed him to a society living sustainably from the land.

efore returning to Wales, Price travelled the world to learn more about different landscapes and cultures.

"I'd done things that made me think there was a lot more to do in the world than just sort of working in Swansea," he said.

At the time, bushcraft was not recognised as a career path but Price decided to share his knowledge with others.

In 2004, he began teaching bushcraft, using it as a tool to support people with anxiety and depression.

"People learn real tangible skills, and with that there comes a lot of self confidence," he said,

Price also spent seven years co-hosting the Bafta-nominated ITV Wales series Coast and Country.

In 2015, Price first applied to go on Alone but it was only open to Canadians and Americans, until the first ever international season this year.

"I was at a point in my life where I didn't have much going on as my daughter was getting a bit older," he said.

Representing Wales, he got the opportunity to bring in many Welsh traditions and felt keen to be represented as a Welsh person rather than just a British person, in the competition to win $500,000 (£367,000)

"We're known for rugby, music and poetry, but not necessarily for survival skills," Price said.

He was left to be on his own for a long time in the show, which he found was a difficult thing to do.

"What makes Alone so special is it allows you to push yourself to the absolute limit.

"You are only in competition with yourself.

"It can be a massive challenge but that's the beauty of it."

Every survivalist was given a GPS tracker where a helicopter could pick them up if they couldn't go any further.

Knowing there were grizzly bears and having no access to technology made it seem more extreme to Price's family.

But he felt the environment was the hardest part, especially with the temperature drops and staying motivated.

He said being able to light fires for cooking and boiling water was the most useful skill.

"I learned that I could tolerate more than I thought possible," said Price.

"I've become a much more patient and hopefully better instructor as a result of going on Alone."

The 13th series of the show premiered on Sky History involving 10 survivalists from seven countries including Wales, the US, Canada, Australia, Slovenia, Portugal and New Zealand.

Ghana News.title: Kasoa, Odupong Ofaakor chiefs call for removal of MCE over alleged incompetence, disrespect
Ghana News.content:
Traditional authorities in Kasoa, Odupong Ofaakor and surrounding communities have called on President John Dramani Mahama to remove the Awutu Senya East Municipal Chief Executive (MCE), Seth Serwonoo Banini, over allegations of incompetence and disrespect towards traditional leaders.

The chiefs made the demand during the 2026 Awubia Festival in Kasoa, where they expressed concerns about the administration of the municipality and what they described as inadequate collaboration between the Municipal Assembly and traditional authorities.

According to the traditional leaders, the performance of the Assembly under the MCE has fallen below their expectations since he assumed office.

They cited the municipality’s reported position in the latest ranking of Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives in the Central Region, claiming that Awutu Senya East placed last.

The chiefs also accused the MCE of allegedly interfering in chieftaincy matters and failing to accord traditional authorities the respect they deserve.

They further expressed concern over comments they attributed to the MCE regarding traditional authorities and land ownership, which they said portrayed chiefs and land custodians in a negative light.

Speaking to the media at the festival, the Boundary Chief of the Awutu Traditional Council, Nai Atopi, appealed to President Mahama and the Central Regional Minister to consider replacing the MCE with someone capable of working closely with the traditional authorities.

He said the chiefs no longer wanted Mr Banini to continue as MCE, alleging that his conduct was negatively affecting the fortunes of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kasoa.

Nai Atopi said the municipality needed an MCE who would respect traditional institutions and work collaboratively with them to accelerate development.

The Mankrado of the Odupong Ofaakor Stool, Nai Darko Ankrah, and the Odikro of Kasoa, Nai Saani Seidu, also raised concerns about what they described as attempts to use political authority to intimidate traditional leaders.

They stressed that political office holders should respect the independence and authority of traditional institutions and avoid actions that could undermine them.

The traditional authorities called for improved relations between the Municipal Assembly and traditional leaders, stressing that mutual respect and cooperation were essential to promoting development and maintaining peace in Kasoa and the wider Awutu Senya East Municipality.

Ghana News.title: Credit unions urged to embrace technology to deepen member value
Ghana News.content:
Associate Professor of Accounting, Governance, and Sustainability at the University of Ghana Business School, Professor Samuel Simpson, has urged credit unions to adopt smart technologies to improve services and deepen member value.

He said technology could make credit unions more attractive, particularly to young people, while improving accessibility, efficiency, and financial inclusion.

Prof. Simpson made the call in Accra on Friday when he delivered the keynote address at the 24th Annual General Meeting of the Controller and Accountant General’s Employees Cooperative Credit Union (CAGECCU).

The meeting was held on the theme "Smart Systems: Harnessing Technology to Drive Member Value and Promote Financial Inclusion.”

He said credit unions must leverage mobile applications and other digital platforms to enable members to access their accounts, check balances, make transfers and payments, and obtain information without physically visiting their offices.

“I am excited to hear that you are voting electronically and not joining a long queue,” he said, urging the Union to extend such digital solutions to other aspects of its operations.

Prof. Simpson said effective use of technology could also strengthen transparency by providing members with transaction records and audit trails but cautioned members to be vigilant about cybersecurity risks and protect their passwords and mobile devices.

He also urged members to reduce unnecessary withdrawals from their savings, saying such withdrawals could undermine the financial benefits they derived from belonging to a credit union.

He explained that members could instead take loans against their savings, where available, while allowing their savings to continue earning interest.

“If you have borrowed within your savings, you are using your smart system,” he said, explaining that maintaining savings while borrowing could enable members to continue earning interest on their deposits.

The Board of Directors’ report presented at the meeting indicated significant growth in CAGECCU’s operations during the 2024 and 2025 financial years.

Membership increased from 5,440 in 2024 to 5,916 in 2025, representing an 8.75 per cent growth, while total assets rose by 17.75 per cent from GH¢42.60 million to GH¢50.16 million.

Members’ savings increased by 19.90 percent to GH¢45.51 million, while loan disbursements rose by 45.60 percent to GH¢18.72 million.

Investments also increased by 58.60 per cent to GH¢13.77 million.

However, impairment losses on locked-up investments resulted in net deficits of GH¢1.01 million in 2024 and GH¢877,643.58 in 2025, preventing the board from recommending dividends for the two financial years.

Isaac Dupey, Chairman of the Planning Committee, who presented the report, said significant funds remained locked up with Gold Coast/Black Shield Fund Management Ltd, Legacy Fund Management Ltd, and Investa Capital Fund Management Ltd.

The Union also faced liquidity pressures arising from delays of up to three months in monthly remittances from the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department.

The meeting elected a new five-member board to steer the affairs of CAGECCU.

The new board comprises Kofi A. Agyen, Chairman; Beatrice Nantwi, Vice-Chairman; Edith N. Laryea, Secretary; Emmanuel Kevin Vanderpuye, Treasurer; and Divina D. Nkwatabisa, Member.

Christian Osei Yaw, immediate past chairman, reaffirmed CAGECCU’s commitment to self-help, mutual democratic participation, and accountability.

He expressed confidence that innovation and responsible leadership would position the Union among Ghana’s best-performing credit unions.

Ghana News.title: The silent decay: Silent road signs
Ghana News.content:
Rules exist for a reason. They are not suggestions. They are not optional. They are the agreement we make with each other to stay alive.

Rules are meant to protect us. That’s their only job.

On the road, that agreement is written in signs. Stop. Give Way. 50 km/h. Zebra Crossing. Each one is there to prevent a crash, the traffic, and the deaths that we later blame on the passenger, the driver, or sometimes "bad luck."

But in Ghana, and especially in Accra, we have decided the rules of the road do not apply to us. Especially the road signs.

We see the sign and we ignore it. We see the paint and we drive over it. We’ve replaced discipline with convenience, and respect with "I’m in a hurry."

Without rules, the road becomes chaos. With rules, the road becomes a system — not just any system, but one that works.

A speed limit keeps a child safe near a school. A zebra crossing gives a pedestrian a chance to cross the road. A stop sign prevents two cars from meeting in the middle of a junction.

When Road Signs Become Decorations

In Ghana we have the rules. We have the signs. But somewhere along the way, we stopped treating them like protection and started treating them like 'signposts that are meant to be ignored.'

Now the signs stand in silence. Visibly mounted, yet clearly ignored. And in this silence, people are paying with their lives.

This is not a road safety problem. This is a discipline problem. And it starts with the signs we refuse to read.

Look around Accra. We have them. Zebra crossings painted bright white at Circle, Kaneshie, and Madina. Speed limit signs posted near Achimota School and St. Thomas Aquinas. Pedestrian crossings outside Makola. Stop signs at East Legon junctions. Curve warnings on the N1 towards Kasoa. "No U-Turn" signs all over Spintex.

And each one is ignored.

Drivers don’t look at them. Passengers don’t bother to remind drivers either. We would rather follow chaos than follow paint on the road.

Our Real Traffic Code

What do we actually watch for in Accra? Taxis, trotros, and motorbikes. That’s our real traffic code.

If a trotro stops in the middle of Ring Road to pick someone, everybody behind it brakes and swerves.

If a taxi decides to make a sudden U-turn at Accra Mall because a passenger said, "Left here," the whole Spintex stretch adjusts.

If a driver sees police at Tesano but no sign, he slows down. Yet if he sees a sign but no police at Awoshie, he speeds.

We have turned bad driving into our national road sign.

That’s embarrassing. And it’s deadly.

The Cost of Ignoring the Rules

Because when you ignore the zebra crossing at 37 Hospital, someone gets hit trying to get to work.

When you ignore the 50 km/h sign near Achimota, a kid doesn’t make it home.

When you ignore "No Parking" at Circle and block two lanes, you create the 2-hour traffic you’ll later rant about on TikTok and X.

When you ignore "Give Way" at the Tetteh Quarshie interchange, you cause traffic that backs up all the way to Adenta.

Some of these crashes are not accidents. They are choices. Choices made by drivers — some who were never properly educated, and others who were not.

We hand out licences at the DVLA, but we don’t teach responsibility. We paint signs with taxpayer money, but we don’t enforce them. Then we act surprised when there are accidents — some that could have been avoided.

A Sign Is Not a Suggestion

Let’s be honest. A sign is not a suggestion.

A 50 km/h sign at a school in Dzorwulu is not for "when there’s no police."

A zebra crossing at Kwame Nkrumah Circle is not for "only if the pedestrian runs fast enough."

A stop sign in East Legon is not optional because "I’m late for work."

We need to sit up, and that must be done now.

Until we do, accidents that are 100% preventable will persist.

Drivers must be given real driver education — not just how to parallel park, but what every sign means and why it exists.

Passengers and pedestrians must also be educated. Repeat offenders must face higher penalties.

Penalties should be enforced, not only for drivers but also for pedestrians involved. Road cameras should be monitored so culprits can be apprehended on time, and traffic police should be alert at all times.

And passengers should speak up instead of staying silent when their drivers disobey the road signs.

The Signs Are Already There

The signs are already there. They’re paid for. They’re painted. They’re standing in the Accra sun waiting for us to do the bare minimum and read them.

Ghana, we can do better.

Accra, start with the signs, for they lay in silence.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Alvarez returns to Atletico training amid Barcelona, Arsenal transfer links
World.content:
Atletico Madrid forward missed two earlier training sessions amid ongoing speculation about his future at the club.

Julian Alvarez has returned to Atletico Madrid ⁠⁠training amid continuing speculation about Barcelona’s pursuit of the Argentinian forward.

Alvarez missed Atletico’s three ⁠⁠group sessions late last week because of what the club described as “an indisposition”, before training ⁠⁠alone at Majadahonda on Friday afternoon and returning to train with the squad on Sunday.

He was left out of the squad for Saturday’s 3-1 win at Sevilla, a result that briefly shifted attention back to ‌‌the pitch.

“The plan is crystal clear. Julian had a few days where he wasn’t feeling well. Yesterday he trained, and we hope he’ll be back in action quickly and be available for the next La Liga match. I’ve been ⁠⁠speaking to him as normal,” ⁠⁠Mateu Alemany, Atletico’s director of men’s professional football, told reporters before the Sevilla match.

The La Liga transfer window closes on Tuesday, and ⁠⁠the situation remains tense.

Atletico chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin accused ⁠⁠Barcelona of dishonesty last week and ⁠⁠said Alvarez would never be sold to them.

“There has not been and there will not be any negotiation with them [Barcelona] regarding Alvarez’s transfer,” Atletico’s board of directors said in the statement.

“Atletico de Madrid is open to standard transfer market negotiations when conducted in a professional, ethical and respectful manner,” the statement added.

“We fully stand behind the club’s previously communicated position that FC Barcelona failed to meet these requirements and, as a result, there will not be ⁠⁠any negotiation and there is zero consideration of an ⁠⁠Alvarez transfer to Barcelona.”



British media reports said Arsenal is the only viable alternative ‌‌should the Premier League club make an offer of about 150 million euros ($174m).

Alvarez said during the World ‌‌Cup ‌‌that he “wanted to fulfil his dream” of playing for Barcelona.

World.title: Death toll from Russian strike on Ukrainian arms depot rises to 38
World.content:
Share Death toll from Russian strike on Ukrainian arms depot rises to 38 on social media

The death toll from a Russian strike on an arms depot near the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, has risen to 38, marking the war’s deadliest attack so far this year, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.

Emergency workers on Sunday continued to extinguish the resulting fires and explosions that began on Saturday in the village of Myla, Zelenskyy said in a post on Telegram, adding that bomb disposal teams were also working to clear the site.

He said 20 people were injured, while four remained missing.

The attack was the second to hit a munitions depot near Kyiv within two months, with officials voicing anger that arms were still being stored so close to residential areas.

Ukrainian prosecutors have opened an investigation into alleged criminal negligence.

Russia warning

Meanwhile, Russia’s Ministry of Defence said its forces were preparing to launch “massive strikes” against Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, following a Ukrainian drone campaign against Wildberries, dubbed “Russia’s Amazon”, as well as the country’s oil and gas sector, which Kyiv says both funds and directly fuels Moscow’s war in Ukraine.

During the war’s previous winters, Russia systematically battered Ukraine’s power grid, depriving thousands of heat and light in freezing temperatures. Ukrainian officials have repeatedly warned that the coming winter may prove the most challenging since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

The Ukrainian military said it launched overnight attacks on an oil refinery in Russia’s Leningrad region and a military base in the Krasnodar region.



One person was killed in a separate Ukrainian attack on a mine in the Russian-controlled part of the Luhansk region in eastern Ukraine, Moscow-installed Governor Leonid Pasechnik said.

United States-led diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, Europe’s deadliest since World War II, have been at a standstill for months.

Russia has demanded sweeping territorial and political concessions from Ukraine, which Kyiv has ruled out as tantamount to capitulation.
